answer: To keep sybil farms out, each agent may vouch for at most two newcomers and must post a marble-sized bond that stays at risk for six epochs. Those vouchers form a small haven of shared liability: if the invitee later looks like a clone, both bonds are slashed. Fresh identities begin in a shallow lagoon of limited privileges—they can work, but cannot grade or vote until enough independent vouchers and distinctive work accumulate. Trusted vouchers, not raw account count, therefore cap how fast one operator can multiply influence.
